selection: nuclear power plant risk cost per kWh
description: Monte-Carlo estimate of the expected accident (severe core damage) risk cost of a new large light-water reactor, expressed in Rappen per kWh, computed under four widths of the 95% confidence interval on the two dominant uncertain inputs: the core damage frequency per reactor-year and the total accident damage cost. Build cost, lifetime energy production, core damage frequency band and Fukushima-scale damage cost are sourced (measured value); the CI widths and the damage-cost median are modelling assumptions (assumed value with confidence). All derived per-kWh figures are tagged assumed value because they depend on the assumed CI widths.

formulas.name: accident probability over lifetime (formula)
formulas.description: cumulative probability of at least one severe core damage accident over the operating lifetime, from the annual core damage frequency and the lifetime in years.

formulas.name: expected risk cost (formula)
formulas.expression: "expected risk cost" = "accident probability over lifetime" * "accident damage cost"
formulas.description: point-estimate expected accident risk cost as the product of lifetime accident probability and accident damage cost; the Monte Carlo mean differs from this because both inputs are uncertain and the product is right-skewed.

formulas.name: risk cost per kWh (formula)
formulas.expression: "risk cost per kWh" = "expected risk cost" * 100000000000 / "lifetime energy production"
formulas.description: converts the expected risk cost in billion CHF to Rappen per kWh by multiplying by 1e9 (billion to CHF) times 100 (CHF to Rappen) and dividing by the lifetime energy production in kWh.

sources.name: IWR Hinkley Point C cost 2026
sources.description: Internationales Wirtschaftsforum Regenerative Energien, 23 Feb 2026: Hinkley Point C build cost revised to about GBP 48bn (2026 prices), roughly EUR 55bn for two 1600 MW EPR blocks, i.e. about EUR 27.5bn per 1600 MW block.

sources.name: EC 2003 core damage frequency
sources.description: 2003 European Commission study, reported via Core damage frequency (Wikipedia): core damage frequencies of 5e-5 per reactor-year are a common result, i.e. one core damage incident in about 20,000 reactor-years.

sources.name: EPRI 2008 core damage frequency
sources.description: 2008 Electric Power Research Institute study, reported via Core damage frequency (Wikipedia): estimated core damage frequency for the US nuclear industry about 2e-5 per reactor-year, i.e. one in 50,000 reactor-years.

sources.name: Sornette 2012 empirical CDF
sources.description: Exploring the limits of safety analysis in complex technological systems (arXiv:1207.5674): a conservative light-water-reactor core damage frequency figure of 1e-4 per reactor-year is consistent with roughly one such event over the 10,000 to 15,000 reactor-years of nuclear plant history.

sources.name: METI 2016 Fukushima cost
sources.description: Japan Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry, Dec 2016: total Fukushima disaster cost estimate raised to 21.5 trillion yen, about USD 188 billion, including decommissioning, compensation and decontamination.

sources.name: JCER 2019 Fukushima cost
sources.description: Japan Center for Economic Research, 2019: total Fukushima cleanup and compensation cost estimated between 35 and 81 trillion yen, about USD 470 to 660 billion, well above the government estimate.

sources.name: zukunft.com Monte Carlo simulation 2026-07-05
sources.description: Monte Carlo simulation (4,000,000 draws, lognormal inputs clipped to [0,1] for probability), computed for this analysis: annual core damage frequency and accident damage cost drawn from lognormal distributions calibrated so the 95% CI equals [median/factor, median*factor]; lifetime accident probability and per-kWh risk cost derived per draw. CDF median 1e-4 per reactor-year, damage-cost median 300 bn CHF, lifetime 60 years, net capacity 1600 MW, capacity factor 0.90.

calc-validation.note: 1 - (1 - 1e-4)^60 = 0.005983; rounds to 0.01 at 2 decimals. Point-estimate lifetime accident probability, independent of the CI width.
